gaps.note: Monad. Cycle 10 settled the compiled multiplication paths by transcription (theme-monad-compiled-mul), but the compiled code that decides settlement is still unread and untested: RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY after the balanceOf STATICCALL of Currency.balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) and after the transfer CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), CALLVALUE in _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:352-356), TLOAD and TSTORE of CurrencyReserves and CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39), the KECCAK256 runtime helper that forms every delta slot, and SIGNEXTEND with a variable index. Simulated calls on Monad always use the interpreter (OPCODES.md:111), so the 550 scripts and the 185,529 vectors say nothing about these compiled paths, and mined evidence on Monad covers only Swap events. No unit has compared a mined Monad receipt with an independent re-execution, which the MegaETH unit did for 7,627 transactions.

HyperEVM. Lead L-547 lists HyperEVM, and the hyperevm unit did not answer it: no mined transaction with a reverted unlock frame followed by a completed unlock was checked against re-execution. The cleared item 'Step trace of the archive client' rests on the statement that the archive client verifies headers against the validator's blocks, so a divergence would have stopped it. No source for that statement was fetched. The nanoreth README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/README.md, fetched 2026-11-24) says system transactions arrive from hl-node unsigned and that nanoreth fabricates their signatures, which shows it ingests the validator's block data; it does not say that nanoreth compares its own state root or receipts root with the validator's header.

MegaETH. The finding of theme-megaeth-executor shows the block producer is a closed JIT executor and RPC replicas apply its results without re-execution. The evidence for that executor is 53,811 Swap events, 2,885 replays and 7,627 receipts compared by logs and status. Liquidity removals, fee collections, ERC-6909 burns and any sync, settle or take inside a reverted frame were not observed. The public stateless validator, the only public re-execution that compares full post-state, was not run (the unit's own medium lead).

All 21 networks. Mined evidence is limited to Swap events. ModifyLiquidity events carry no amounts (OPCODES.md:202), so the amounts that block production paid to liquidity providers who removed liquidity or collected fees (Pool.modifyLiquidity, Position.update at src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96, SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta) have never been checked on any network. On Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM, where block execution runs a path that eth_call does not, this is the withdrawal path of the victims the review protects, and it is checked only by simulated calls.

Keccak cache in front of KECCAK256. stablecoin-l1 found that Tempo and Arc route KECCAK256 through the alloy-primitives process-wide cache (feature keccak-cache-global, fixed-cache 0.1.10 and 0.1.8) and read it for Tempo and Arc only. The op-reth v2.9.0 lockfile also pins alloy-primitives 1.7.3 with fixed-cache 0.1.10 as a dependency (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.9.0/rust/Cargo.lock, fetched 2026-11-24, lines 635-646 and 5259-5260), and the Base v1.5.6 lockfile pins fixed-cache 0.1.10 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/Cargo.lock, line 9775). Whether these binaries turn the global cache on was not read. Polygon's separate 64 byte cache was read in cycle 8.

Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium. Cycle 10 covered these networks only through the Go toolchain theme. The release the endpoints report, nitro v3.13.0-rc.9, is still not public, Elysium's build names no version, and L-547 and L-617 for Elysium remain open.

Celo, X Layer, Ethereum and Avalanche had no network unit in cycle 10 apart from the Go theme for Avalanche. X Layer pins ruint 1.18.0 (OPCODES.md:132), the oldest of the reth based nodes, and is inside the range of advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0220 that theme-megaeth-executor cleared for MegaETH's revm v112 only. Celo's endpoint serves two clients and L-604 (celo-kona moving to revm-interpreter 42.0.0) is unanswered.

Unichain. The op-stack-eth verifier compared the deployed bytecode of six of the seven OP chains with Ethereum. The seventh, Unichain's 24,050 byte genesis predeploy at 0x1f98400000000000000000000000000000000004, has different bytes and has still never run any of the 550 scripts (L-584, L-426 open since cycle 8).

Polygon. Block producers run BlockSTM parallel execution, while the RPC answers eth_call serially. The cycle 3 clearance of transient storage under Bor's parallel executor rests on reading. The receipt against re-execution method of theme-megaeth-executor (frames.py) has not been applied to Polygon.

leads.question: Monad serves debug_traceTransaction with callTracer and withLog (queried 2026-11-24 on https://rpc.monad.xyz, block 0x7736952), and its docs say it has no opcode level struct logs (https://docs.monad.xyz/reference/json-rpc/overview.md). Does that trace re-execute the transaction in the interpreter, or return call frames recorded during block execution? If it re-executes, apply frames.py of theme-megaeth-executor to mined Monad PoolManager transactions that call sync, settle, settleFor, take, mint or burn, or that hold a reverted unlock frame followed by a completed unlock, and compare receipt status and logs with the trace. If it does not re-execute, compare the receipts with eth_call of the same transaction at the parent block for transactions at index 0 of their block.
leads.why: Block execution on Monad runs the PoolManager as compiled code that no simulated call reaches. A compiled fault in TSTORE rollback, CALLVALUE or return data handling on the settlement path (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) would credit a payer who did not pay, which is theft by an ordinary account from every pool of that currency. Nothing so far tests this path in blocks.

leads.question: Transcribe the Monad v0.16.5 x86 code generation and runtime helpers for RETURNDATASIZE, RETURNDATACOPY, CALLVALUE, TLOAD, TSTORE, KECCAK256 and SIGNEXTEND with a variable index, at each operand location the emitter distinguishes, and run them on the exact instruction sequences of Currency.transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95), CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) as they appear in build/PoolManager.json. Do any operands give a result other than the specification?
leads.why: These are the compiled paths that decide how much a settler is credited and whether a payout succeeded. A wrong return data length or a stale transient word there would let an ordinary account take pooled tokens without paying. This replaces the open remainder of L-599.

leads.question: For mined ModifyLiquidity events with negative liquidityDelta or zero liquidityDelta (fee collection) on these five networks, reconstruct the amounts block production paid from the ERC-20 Transfer events and native value transfers of the same transaction (or from the PositionManager's ERC-721 position state), and compare them with SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol) and the fee formula of Position.update (src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96) at the pool state of the parent block. Do any differ by more than the rounding the source allows?
leads.why: Liquidity removal is how the victims of this review withdraw, and no network has a mined check of its amounts (OPCODES.md:202). On Monad and MegaETH block execution runs compiled code and on HyperEVM a closed validator, so an overpayment to a remover there would be invisible to every simulated test so far.

leads.question: Run the public MegaETH stateless validator (mega-evm v1.7.3 on revm 40.0.3) over a range of mainnet blocks that holds PoolManager swaps, liquidity removals, fee collections and the 1,333 quoter pattern transactions found in cycle 10. Does any block give a state root mismatch? In the same range, list every transaction in which sync, settle, settleFor or take ran inside a reverted frame and compare receipt with re-execution as frames.py does.
leads.why: Receipts and logs were compared, but storage and transient effects were not. A credit kept from a reverted payment frame, or a wrong storage write from the closed JIT executor, is the path by which an ordinary account could take funds without paying. The unit marked the reverted settle question low; it is the only open rollback case that leads to theft.

leads.question: Does nanoreth or hyper-evm-sync compute the state root and receipts root of each HyperEVM block and compare them with the header that hl-node produced, and does it stop on a mismatch? Find the code that does it in their source on raw.githubusercontent.com. Then answer L-547 for HyperEVM: find one mined transaction with a reverted unlock frame followed by a completed unlock, and one with settle or take in a reverted frame, and compare the validator's receipt with nanoreth's debug_traceTransaction.
leads.why: The HyperEVM validator is closed, and the cycle 10 clearance of its execution rests on a claim that the archive client would have stopped on a divergence. If the archive client only ingests the validator's output, nothing public checks the validator's storage writes or transient rollback, and every HyperEVM clearance outside Swap events is unsupported.

leads.question: Do op-reth v2.9.0 and v2.8.1, base v1.5.6, world-chain v2.8.2, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, xlayer v0.0.7, reth v2.11.0 and the public MegaETH stateless validator enable the alloy-primitives feature keccak-cache-global in their binary crates, and with which fixed-cache version and configuration (LOCK_FREE_READS, EPOCHS)? For each that does, reread the get and insert paths as stablecoin-l1 did for fixed-cache 0.1.10.
leads.why: The cache sits in front of every KECCAK256 of 1 to 87 bytes, which covers every mapping slot and every transient delta slot of the PoolManager. It was read only for Tempo and Arc. A torn read would place a delta or a balance at another account's slot.

leads.question: Apply frames.py to mined Polygon PoolManager transactions in blocks produced with BlockSTM: for transactions with a reverted unlock frame followed by a completed unlock, and for transactions that call sync or settle, do receipt status and logs equal debug_traceTransaction re-execution on a serial node?
leads.why: Parallel execution in block production and serial execution on the RPC are two code paths, and the transient storage clearance for Bor's parallel executor rests on reading.
